name: Chin tuck
why: Wakes up the deep muscles at the front of your neck that hold your head balanced over your shoulders. After long hours at a screen the head drifts forward and these muscles switch off, which loads the back of the neck.
setup: Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed.
Look straight ahead with your chin level.
mistakes: Tipping the chin down to the chest instead of sliding the head back
Pushing so hard that the neck strains
feel: A gentle stretch at the base of your skull and light effort at the front of your neck.
stopIf: Pain spreads into your arm, or you feel dizzy, tingly or numb.

name: Deep neck flexor nod
why: Trains the deep neck flexors with a tiny nodding movement. Building their endurance like this reduces neck pain and neck-related headaches. Work up to 10-second holds.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent. Use a thin folded towel under your head if your chin pokes up.
Relax your jaw and rest your tongue on the roof of your mouth.
cues: Nod as if saying a small yes
Keep the back of the neck long
Front of the neck stays soft
mistakes: Lifting the head off the floor
Jamming the chin into the chest
Tensing the big muscles at the front of the neck
feel: A light effort deep at the front of the neck, under the chin.
stopIf: Neck pain increases, or you feel dizzy.
references: Jull G, et al. 2002. A randomized controlled trial of exercise and manipulative therapy for cervicogenic headache. Spine 27:1835-43.

name: Neck rotation
why: Gentle, regular movement keeps a stiff neck moving and is often the quickest way to ease morning stiffness.
setup: Sit tall with your shoulders relaxed.
cues: Turn your head slowly to one side
Only as far as is comfortable
Back to the middle, then the other way
mistakes: Lifting the shoulders as you turn
Forcing the end of the range
feel: Gentle movement and a light stretch in the neck.
stopIf: Dizziness, blurred vision, or pain spreading into the arm.

name: Upper trapezius stretch
why: Eases tightness along the side of the neck and top of the shoulder, where tension builds up with stress, desk work and carrying bags.
setup: Sit tall and hold the side of the chair seat with your right hand to keep that shoulder down.
Slowly tilt your left ear towards your left shoulder.
Optional: rest your left hand on your head for a little extra weight. Don't pull.
mistakes: Letting the stretched-side shoulder creep up
Turning the head instead of tilting it
feel: A stretch along the side of the neck into the top of the shoulder, on the side away from the tilt.
stopIf: Pain or tingling travels down your arm, or you feel dizzy.

name: Levator scapulae stretch
why: Stretches the muscle that runs from the side of the neck to the top of the shoulder blade, a common source of the 'knot' at the base of the neck.
setup: Sit tall and hold the chair seat with your right hand.
Turn your nose towards your left armpit, then let your head drop gently forward.
feel: A stretch from the back of the neck down towards the top of the shoulder blade, on the side away from your nose.
stopIf: Pain or tingling into the arm, or dizziness.

name: Shoulder blade squeeze
why: Wakes up the muscles between your shoulder blades that get lazy when you sit rounded at a desk, taking strain off the neck and shoulders.
setup: Sit or stand tall with your arms relaxed by your sides.
cues: Squeeze shoulder blades back and down
feel: Effort between and below your shoulder blades.
